title: Open Agent Protocol extension pack descriptor
description: A pack.json: what an extension pack defines, declared rather than inferred from its schemas, so containment can be checked before anything is compiled. Shape only; the namespace, containment, prefix-freedom, gate, role, and reference rules are checked by the loader, which refuses the pack rather than diagnosing a trace.

id.description: The pack's namespace: a reverse-DNS name. The unprefixed namespace is the spec's, in its entirety.

schemas.description: The schema files the pack contributes, each a relative path contained beneath the pack root.

depends_on.description: The packs whose resources this pack's schemas may $ref. A dependency is satisfied only by a loaded pack of that exact id and version.

role.description: Stated, never inferred: a request and an event both omit in_reply_to and need opposite treatment under an unadvertised key.

schema.description: The branch this type contributes to the envelope union, as <file>#<pointer> into one of the pack's own schemas. The branch must pin type to a const naming this type.

replies_to.description: For a response: the declared request of this pack that it answers. A response takes its gate from that request and carries no gate of its own.

refusals.description: For a request: the pack's own error codes the endpoint may answer it with for domain reasons. A refusal outside the declared set is unhonoured_capability.

gates.description: From each declared request and event, and each member the pack adds to a core payload, to the capability key that must be advertised for it. Stated for every one of them: a missing entry is a load refusal, not a silent hole.

payload_members.description: Members the pack adds to core payloads. A member has no branch of its own, so the subschema its value must satisfy is declared here and judged in a pass of its own; the core payload is never patched.

fixtures.description: The pack's own fixture manifest, in the core manifest format, contained beneath the pack root. Its entries claim the pack's ext: term and never a core unit.

relativePath.description: A path the loader cleans, joins beneath the pack root, and resolves symlinks for. Shape alone cannot decide containment — a symlink is a relative path that leaves the root — so the rule has one home, in the loader.
